name: intraday_vol_pattern_v1
author: claude-4.6-opus-fast
thesis: Intraday volatility follows a well-documented U-shape pattern: high at open (09:15-10:00), declining through lunch (11:30-13:30), and rising again toward close (14:30-15:30). This pattern is exploitable because momentum strategies (BUY_CE/BUY_PE in trend direction) work best during high-vol periods (open, close) while mean-reversion works during low-vol periods (lunch). Additionally, the transition from low-vol to high-vol in the afternoon (13:30-14:00) creates a predictable volatility expansion that can be traded with directional option positions. The inefficiency exists because most strategies ignore the time-of-day vol structure, applying the same logic at 10:00 AM and 2:00 PM despite vastly different volatility environments.
indicators: expected_vol = 20d_avg_vol_at_this_5s_bar  # seasonal vol expectation at 5s resolution
session_period = 'open' if time < 10:00 else 'mid_morning' if time < 11:30 else 'lunch' if time < 13:30 else 'afternoon' if time < 14:30 else 'close'
ATR_120 = ATR(high, low, close, 120)  # 120 bars = 10 min at 5s

conditions: IF session_period == 'lunch': close < BB_lower_240 AND vol_surprise < 0.8 (mean_rev in low vol)
IF session_period == 'open' OR 'close': close > EMA_60 AND EMA_60 > EMA_156 AND vol_surprise > 1.2 (momentum in high vol)
IF session_period == 'afternoon': close > BB_mid_240 AND vol_surprise starting to rise from <0.8 to >1.0 (vol expansion entry)
long.confirmation: lunch: RSI(168) < 30 upticks; open/close: new 240-bar high; afternoon: vol_surprise crosses 1.0 from below

conditions: IF session_period == 'lunch': close > BB_upper_240 AND vol_surprise < 0.8
IF session_period == 'open' OR 'close': close < EMA_60 AND EMA_60 < EMA_156 AND vol_surprise > 1.2
IF session_period == 'afternoon': close < BB_mid_240 AND vol_surprise starting to rise
short.confirmation: lunch: RSI(168) > 70 downticks; open/close: new 240-bar low; afternoon: vol_surprise crosses 1.0

entry.entry_price: limit order on option (lunch period) or market order on option (open/close period)

exit.target: lunch: BB_mid_240 (mean rev target); open/close: 1.5 * ATR_120; afternoon: 1.0 * ATR_120
exit.stop_loss: lunch: 0.3 * ATR_120 beyond BB; open/close: 0.8 * ATR_120; afternoon: 0.5 * ATR_120
exit.trailing_stop: open/close: after 1.0 * ATR_120, trail at 0.5 * ATR_120; others: none
exit.signal_exit: if session_period transitions while in trade, re-evaluate using new period's exit rules

risk.position_sizing: vol-scaled: base_size * (median_expected_vol / current_expected_vol) to equalize risk across periods

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 for lunch mean-rev; no VIX filter for open/close momentum
filters.time_filter: strategy is time-of-day by design; each period has its own filter
filters.volume_filter: option volume must be within 50-200% of expected_volume_at_this_time
filters.trend_filter: lunch: ADX < 25; open/close: ADX > 18; afternoon: no ADX filter
filters.event_filter: skip if major news event disrupts the normal vol pattern (VIX > 25)
other_filters: verify U-shape pattern exists for this index on trailing 20 days before trading

edge.edge_decay_risk: low -- the intraday vol U-shape is a structural market microstructure feature documented across all major markets

mechanism: At 5-second frequency, the vol U-shape creates micro-opportunities invisible at 1-minute resolution. During the open period, 5s bars capture the initial burst of volatility and allow entering momentum option trades (BUY_CE/BUY_PE) at the exact moment of directional breakout rather than waiting for a full 1-minute bar to close. During the lunch lull, 5s bars detect the precise BB touch and reversal, allowing tighter mean-reversion entries on option premium. The afternoon vol expansion signal (vol_surprise crossing 1.0 from below) at 5s resolution gives a 20-40 second head start over 1-min detection, critical for capturing the initial premium spike as volatility re-emerges.
adaptation_notes: Adapted from 1-min equity strategy to 5-sec index option strategy. Key changes: (1) Universe changed from NIFTY50 constituent stocks to NIFTY50/BANKNIFTY index options (BUY_CE/BUY_PE), (2) All indicator lookbacks multiplied by 12x for 5s equivalence: BB(20)->BB(240), EMA(5)->EMA(60), EMA(13)->EMA(156), ATR(10)->ATR(120), RSI(14)->RSI(168), (3) Rolling vol window adjusted from 15 bars to 180 bars (same 15-min window at 5s), (4) Expected vol profile now at 5s resolution (20d_avg_vol_by_5s_bar), (5) Hold time compressed from 10-45 minutes to 5-60 seconds -- scalping option premium reaction to vol regime shifts, (6) Entry/exit now reference option premium (BUY_CE/BUY_PE) instead of equity BUY/SHORT, (7) Removed stock_filter as we trade index options directly.
weaknesses: The strategy effectively runs 3 different sub-strategies (mean-rev, momentum, vol-expansion) which triples the parameter count and overfitting risk compared to a single-regime strategy
On event days (earnings, macro announcements), the U-shape vol pattern is disrupted and all three sub-strategies can simultaneously fail
The afternoon vol-expansion entry (13:30-14:00) has the lowest win rate because the vol rise isn't always directional -- sometimes vol rises but price just chops
prior_art: Wood, McInish & Ord (1985) intraday return volatility patterns; Andersen & Bollerslev (1997) intraday vol seasonality. U-shape in Indian markets confirmed by Sinha (2016).
notes: Adapted for 5-second NIFTY50/BANKNIFTY index option trading. Edge math: 0.60 * 42bps - 0.40 * 28bps = 25.2 - 11.2 = 14bps gross. The time-of-day decomposition adds ~4bps over a static strategy by matching strategy type to vol regime.
